title: Boosted decision tree enables first observation of two simultaneously longitudinally polarized Z bosons
summary: Using 164 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton–proton data and a statistical combination with the Run 2 measurement, ATLAS reports the first observation of ZZ production with both Z bosons longitudinally polarized, at 6.5σ observed (5.6σ expected). The combined signal strength is 1.22 ± 0.21; the Run 3 measurement also reports polarization fractions across the fiducial phase space and two four-lepton invariant-mass ranges, consistent with Standard Model predictions.

evidence.tested: Using 164 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV proton–proton data and a statistical combination with the Run 2 measurement, ATLAS reports the first observation of ZZ production with both Z bosons longitudinally polarized, at 6.5σ observed (5.6σ expected).
evidence.unknown: The ATLAS paper was submitted to PRL as a preprint on 2026-07-14; the cited official ATLAS briefing is dated 2026-08-04. The 6.5σ first observation combines the Run 3 analysis with the prior Run 2 measurement, whose standalone significance was 4.3σ. The Run 3 analysis alone reports 5.1σ. The measured fractions agree with the Standard Model; the statistical uncertainty dominates and polarization-template modeling is the leading systematic uncertainty. This is an experimental observation from ATLAS data, not evidence of physics beyond the Standard Model.
evidence.ai_role: The BDT is trained on polarization-sensitive lepton angular observables to separate longitudinal-longitudinal ZZ events from transverse or mixed-polarization events. Its score distribution is the fitted observable used to extract the signal strength and significance.
